title: Simulated multi-tenant continuous-batch + queueing harness for mixed workload p95/throughput analysis
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a reproducible, parameterized harness that simulates multi-tenant traffic mixes to quantify interactions between continuous batching and request queueing. Focus measurements on tokens/sec (aggregate and per-tenant class), p95 latency per class, and automated regression detection across commits. The harness should support configurable arrival patterns (Poisson, bursty, diurnal), tenant mixes (percent read vs generate, short vs long sequences), and runtime flags (batching window size, max queue depth, KV cache enabled/disabled).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run deterministic scenario definitions from YAML and produce CSV/JSON metrics
Benchmarks report aggregate tokens/sec and p95 per tenant class with 95% confidence intervals
Regression job in CI triggers if p95 increases > 10% for any tenant class compared to baseline
Artifacts (PR, confluence spec, dashboard) are linked and reproducible by other engs
experiment_plan: Define tenant classes: interactive-short (<=128 tokens), background-long (>=1024 tokens), embedding-like (fixed small token sequences)
Implement arrival profiles: uniform, Poisson (lambda tunable), burst (clusters of high arrival), and mixed diurnal curve
Run matrix over batching config: continuous-batching enabled with window 5ms/10ms/20ms, disabled, and greedy max-batch-size settings
Vary queueing thresholds: max-queue-depth 50/200/500 and backpressure behavior (drop, reject, block)
Measure per-run: total tokens emitted, tokens/sec, mean latency, p50/p90/p95/p99, tail-token latency, and CPU/GPU utilization
implementation_details: Harness in Go to reuse existing load generator library used in ENG-6281
Scenario definitions stored in YAML in /bench/scenarios/ with seedable RNG to ensure repeatability
Integrate with our Prometheus test cluster to collect runtime-level metrics and export to a temp Grafana dashboard
Output generator will write run-level JSON with metadata and a CSV timeseries of rolling p95 computed at 30s windows
Regression detection uses a lightweight delta-checker comparing persisted baseline metrics in S3 and annotates CI runs with pass/fail
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with runtime and infra. Decided to model three tenant classes and restrict initial experiments to two GPU types (A100-80G and H100-80G emulation).
2026-03-02: PoC generator implemented for Poisson and burst arrivals. Local runs produce stable tokens/sec for homogeneous traffic. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/112

2026-03-05: First mixed workload run (60% interactive-short, 30% background-long, 10% embedding-like) with continuous-batching=10ms. Observed aggregate tokens/sec = 1.8M, p95 interactive-short = 32ms, p95 background-long = 420ms. Uploaded raw traces to s3://redwood-bench/eng-24765/run-20260305.tar.gz

2026-03-09: Discovered non-linear p95 amplification for background-long when queue depth exceeded 200. Root cause hypothesis: long sequences occupy KV cache eviction windows and reduce effective batching for short sequences. Created ENG-24801 to follow up on KV cache eviction telemetry

2026-03-11: Integrated CI regression checker. Seeded baseline from run 2026-03-05. Configured alert if any p95 per-class increases by >10% over baseline. CI job: bench/continuous/regression (https://ci.redwood.internal/bench/24765)
decisions: Use Poisson as default arrival model for scheduled CI runs; allow burst and diurnal variants for targeted investigations
Report p95 per tenant class rather than only global p95 to avoid masking regressions in small but latency-sensitive classes
Implement regression check threshold at 10% p95 increase initially; tune after 3 full runs across hardware variants
Prefer non-blocking backpressure with controlled rejections for experiments; blocking mode reserved for SLA-simulation runs
risks: CV: Run-to-run variance in mixed workloads could produce false positives in regression detection if baselines are not sufficiently averaged
Telemetry: current KV cache metrics are coarse; need finer eviction/usage counters (see ENG-24801)
Cost: large matrix across hardware x batching x queueing configs could be expensive on perf cluster; budget gating required
Reproducibility: changes in model binary builds or quantization can shift baselines; lock model versions in scenario metadata
next_steps: Add KV cache micro-metrics to harness and coordinate with infra to expose per-session cache hit/miss rates (owner: Clara Nguyen)
Run full matrix (3 batching windows x 3 queue depths x 2 hardware) and upload aggregated results by 2026-03-18
Stabilize baseline by averaging 5 runs per config and store in S3 as canonical baseline
Create customer-facing summary doc highlighting expected p95 ranges and recommendations for batching/queue settings (owner: Benji Morales)
